tools.description: Compute the globally least-time (least-cost) composition path from 'start' to 'goal' over a directed weighted service graph, plus the eikonal potential T(v) for every node and a dual optimality certificate. Two shapes are accepted and may be mixed: (a) [u, v, weight] where weight is the already-blended non-negative refractive index n(u,v); or (b) {from,to, cost?, latency?, reputation?} where the index is derived as a*cost + b*(latency/scale) + c*(1-reputation) using 'blend'. A bare [u, v] is weight 0.

Both holding proves the path is globally optimal — checked in O(E), no Dijkstra, no trust in the oracle.

tools.description: Analyse a network's systemic cascade risk. Treats the exposure graph as an abelian sandpile, drives `grains` unit shocks on a committed pseudo-random schedule, and stabilises after each via a topple queue. Returns the avalanche size distribution, the MLE power-law exponent tau + KS fit, the mean and tail (VaR/CVaR 95% & 99%) avalanche size, the top trigger nodes, a config_commitment and the committed seed for trustless replay. Small tau / heavy tail = one default ripples across the whole market.

tools.description: Audit a computation's thermodynamic cost. Reversible gates (not, copy/fanout, swap, cnot, toffoli, fredkin, input, output) erase 0 bits; boolean reductions (and, or, nand, mux, add, ...) erase fan_in-1 bits; width-erasers (erase, reset, measure, ...) erase 'width' bits.

tools.description: Solve the discrete optimal-transport problem from source distribution a to sink distribution b under ground cost C (or points + metric/p). Returns the optimal transport plan, the cost, the p-Wasserstein distance (when the cost is a p-th power of a metric), and the Kantorovich dual potentials (u, v) — the certificate. method='exact' (default) is solved by min-cost flow and is certifiable; method='sinkhorn' is an explicitly approximate entropic upper bound carrying its regulariser eps.

b.description: Sink distribution weights (len n; renormalised to sum 1).

tools.description: Trustless verification of an optimal-transport cost via a TWO-SIDED primal-dual certificate. Given a, b, C (or points), a claimed_cost, the transport plan P and the Kantorovich potentials (u, v), checks PRIMAL FEASIBILITY (P>=0, row-sums==a, col-sums==b) with <P,C> == claimed_cost (an upper bound) AND DUAL FEASIBILITY u_i + v_j <= C_ij on every (i,j) with claimed_cost == sum a_i u_i + sum b_j v_j (a lower bound). Both bounds meeting at claimed_cost certifies the exact optimum; a dual-only check would accept an under-reported cost. Checked in O(m*n), no re-solve, no trust.

cost.description: Explicit m*n ground-cost matrix C (non-negative). Mutually exclusive with points.

plan.description: Primal transport plan P (m*n, row-sums==a, col-sums==b, P>=0). Required by kantor.verify: it upper-bounds the optimum so a dual-only cert can't under-report.

potentials.description: Kantorovich dual potentials: u over sources (len m), v over sinks (len n).

sink_points.description: Point coordinates (k-D); the cost matrix is derived via 'metric' and 'p'.

source_points.description: Point coordinates (k-D); the cost matrix is derived via 'metric' and 'p'.

tol.description: Relative tolerance (scaled by max|C| for cost checks) for feasibility, duality and the primal-cost match.

tools.description: Trustless eigenpair certificate. Given the graph and a claimed (λ, x), checks the eigen-relation ‖L x − λ x‖ / ‖x‖ ≤ tol and that x is orthogonal to the trivial λ₁ eigenvector (a genuinely non-trivial mode). This certifies in O(E) that λ is a valid non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalue, hence λ ≥ λ₂ — a certified UPPER BOUND on the algebraic connectivity (lambda2_upper_bound), NOT a proof that λ equals the Fiedler value. No full eigendecomposition, no trust in the oracle.
